utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Before we call in the witness, there are a number of matters to be raised. I understand that the Prosecutor has some matters to raise and the Chamber has two matters that it also wishes to raise. So who goes first? I think we will go first. I will not play the game of seeing who asks for an adjournment. You recall that I raised with the parties at the last session the importance to the proper functioning of the Chamber of having documents translated in both working languages. We have been getting the documents only in English, the exhibits. There is of course a requirement that exhibits be produced in the two working languages. The Chamber cannot pretend to be unaware of the difficulties that parties experience in getting documents from the translation unit in a timely manner, but we have to be pragmatic. The Chamber feels that an approach that should be considered will be to have the Prosecutor identify a core bundle of exhibits and have those exhibits translated. I'm aware that we have preadmitted I think some three bundles with over 300 exhibits. What we want the Prosecutor to do is to identify a core set of exhibits from that bundle and see to it that those documents, those exhibits, are translated in a timely manner. This is a matter of the utmost importance to the effective functioning of the Chamber. The other matter that I wanted to raise is that the Chamber has been reviewing the progress of the case. While we cannot say that parties have been working unproductively, we observe that after two weeks, we are only on the sixth witness. The Chamber will, with the cooperation of the interpreters, sit late this week, until 5.00, and on Friday, we will start at 9.00 in the morning. The witnesses testified to a number of different incidents and so the examination-in-chief is relatively long and the cross-examination involves three accused persons. So although we have a relatively short witness list, relative in terms of the Tribunal's experience, we will find that we will have to be inventive and creative and be willing to work longer hours if we are to meet our timetable. Mr. Prosecutor, what do you have to say in relation to these matters? First you and then the other counsel, in so far as they are affected.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I might say that the second issue raised by the court is exactly the first issue that the Prosecution wanted to draw to the court's attention as well. And that is that our concern is that although the time that was scheduled for the Prosecution case in this matter seemed very reasonable when it was first given, after the first two weeks, when we had hoped to have finished our 14th witness, we now are still in the middle of our sixth. We realise that matters are not progressing as quickly as they originally had, perhaps optimistically, been predicted to proceed. I might say that by our calculation, and before today's new schedule came in, we had 32.5 days left and there are a number of witnesses, and we are going to run out of time with 16 witnesses left to go if we continue on our present schedule. Having said that, we have done an analysis very briefly of the first six witnesses -- five witnesses that were completed, and the reason I'm raising this now is it seems that at least for the last three witnesses, there appears to be somewhat of an absence of coordination by Defence counsel of their cross-examination. They are taking considerably more time than are the Prosecution, and the Prosecution have to lead all of the evidence. Hopefully the accused's counsel will be able to focus on that part of the evidence that relates to their clients. We realise that there are going to be areas of background which would relate to all of them, but hopefully there could be some coordination of the cross whereby not each counsel covers each topic again and again and again from the beginning. For example, with Witness C, the Prosecution took 2 hours and 28 minutes, and by our calculation the total Defence time was 3 hours and 54 minutes. For Witness D, the Prosecution took 2 hours and 12 minutes and the Defence collectively took 4 hours and 18 minutes. With Witness E, the Prosecution took 1 hour and 43 minutes, and collectively the Defence took 3 hours and 4 minutes. Now, I realise that we're not here to try to curb Defence. They have legitimate areas for cross-examination and it's in the Court's hands in terms of the amount of latitude that is given, but my concern is simply that if we continue at this pace without coordination by the Defence of their cross-examination, we're going to be hearing these kinds of statistics continue, and we're simply going to run out of time. That is a concern. The second thing, still related to time, is that I recall Your Honour asking us to provide witness summaries, and it's taken a great deal of time and effort for us to produce those, including the sourcing where each allegation comes from, but the payoff is supposed to be that the Defence would be able to indicate to us which areas they would allow us to lead, and we would hopefully be able to utilise the time allotted to us in a more effective manner. Unfortunately, we have not received consistent indication from all three counsel for each witness. One of the counsel has been extremely helpful in indicating to us what paragraphs we can lead on, but until you have consensus from all three, we've got a problem with that. So I suppose what I'm saying is if these summaries are indeed going to be helpful in order to save time, hopefully Defence counsel will be able to give us an indication in advance as to which paragraphs they don't object to as leading from so we can get through the area quicker. Otherwise, I don't know how helpful these summaries are other than to impose yet further work on the Prosecution in order to prepare them and all it does is assist the Defence in sourcing our material, but it there's no economy, unless, of course, it's helpful for the Court, in which case that's a useful function in itself, over and above the time-saving factors. Those are the issues I wanted to deal with with respect to the second point raised and a vital matter to us, because as of the 1st of June, all this time counts against us and we want to make sure that our case is in by then. The second issue about translations, we recognise that due to unforeseen circumstances, these documents now have to be translated into all three languages. The difficulty, as I understand it, is that the French translation department have a finite number of people who have a huge backlog and that it takes a lot of work for them to translate all the documents. We have no control. It's not an OTP function. It is our responsibility to see that these exhibits are provided to the Court in all three languages, but it's not, unfortunately, something over which we have control in the sense that the translation department, as I understand it, does not fall under the OTP. Having said that, Your Honours, we will certainly do our best to identify those core documents and try to get them to translation on a priority basis. Other than do that, I don't know what I can do. I cannot give an undertaking that we have any control over the timely translation. All we can do is comply with your request and hopefully those documents will be available to the Court in a timely fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. But on the last issue first, the Chamber's idea was that you have three bundles with about 350 documents. If you are to identify to the Translation Unit a core set of, say, a hundred, then that's one-third. Of course, the obligation is to have all of them translated, but we're being pragmatic and we want the Court to function as effectively as possible. So that's what the Chamber would like to see you have done, and to the extent that the Chamber is able, the Chamber will bring its authority to bear on this issue to see that these documents are translated. As for the witness summaries, I'll hear from Defence counsel very, very briefly. The summaries are facilitative and the Chamber finds them very useful. One virtue of the summaries is that, as you say, they allow Defence counsel to identify those paragraphs in respect of which the Prosecutor would be able to lead, and the Chamber wishes to reiterate that counsel should pay due regard to this matter, read the summaries before, and identify those areas in respect of which leading is not a problem. I think you raised an excellent point with regard to the need for more coordination in the cross-examination. The Chamber has observed that some of it is repetitive. I'm aware that each counsel represents an individual accused, but some coordination can and should take place, and the Chamber will insist on that as a time-saving device. Just very briefly, Mr. Greaves, do you have anything to say on these matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: As I go first in the cross-examination, it's very difficult for me to be accused of repetitiveness, I hope. As far as leading from the summaries is concerned, I have been providing my learned friends with a short list of those matters which may be led on, and will continue to do so as far as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I fully accept the criticism, and we shall indeed try to meet together and see how we can cut it shorter. But I do hope that you have in mind that three accused are all faced with completely different situations. The interpretation of some events varies from one accused to the other, from one client to the other, and this is perhaps the reason for the somewhat prolonged time. But we shall nevertheless try to optimise it and to reduce the time needed to the least -- to the shortest possible. But I do not think one can simply add up the time devoted by counsel to cross-examination is the right way to proceed. What the Defence counsel can do is to try to agree on matters which are beyond dispute and where there is no need to go cross-examination for every individual client. Otherwise there are very many individual matters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vucicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I cannot make such a bald statement as my learned counsel to the right, Mr. Greaves. Of course, there was some repetition from this position but I will do my best not ever to happen in the future. We will coordinate. However, your point is extremely astute one, but I think you know equity of arms may be considered on this because when we really do not object -- would not object to the Prosecutor to lead if we could lead on cross, and the witness would give all his answers while the Prosecutor leads, so that because it's -- as I was observing, I didn't think this case was going to come up, but perhaps I will go and review those records, and it seems to me that sometimes the witness' answer of course take more than counsel's questioning. So maybe we ought to address that point, too. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Will you bring the witness in?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: If I might just respond one moment. I do notice that the cross-examination style does attempt to actually -- it's like leading -- not leading a witness but extracting evidence in chief. Defence counsel in cross are permitted to put suggestions to a witness in a leading fashion, my understanding of cross-examination, and that might actually speed up the procedure rather than emulate the Prosecution style of, "And then what happened?" Because we are not allowed to lead. They are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Of course, yes. The Defence is of course permitted. They have an obligation to put their case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be brought in, might I also ask a clarification? You will recall, Your Honour, that two weeks ago you indicated to us that the you want us, for the transcript witnesses that we had proposed in our motion, that we actually distribute, I believe is the word you use. This line of documents that is against the back wall are now in compliance, two copies or three copies in English, two in French, plus copies for Defence counsel. Did you want those filed or do you want them distributed by handing them out into the courtroom? We are in time, we are ready, they are here, but I'd like a clarification of what you meant by "distribute."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just have them distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Is the witness being brought in?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I believe he has been asked to be brought in, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Greaves, you had completed your -- where were you? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I think I had finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, so it's Mr. Petrovic? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: May I just check to see on the progress of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Witness F, you remain subject to your declaration. Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Rodic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness F, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Goran Rodic, one of the Defence counsel for Mr. Dosen, and now I will ask you some questions. During the examination-in-chief, you mentioned the situation towards the end of 1991, and you said that numerous Serb refugees from Croatia arrived in Bosnia. Why did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the war in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, the situation following the elections in 1990, you said that the SDA came out first. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you kept abreast of the developments through the press and radio. Could you tell us what was going on in the political plane in the late 1991 and early 1992 in Bosnia, and Prijedor specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say that because I was not a politician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't think you were one. I simply thought that if you listened to the media, you would have to say something more specific.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really wouldn't be able to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also during the direct examination, you referred to certain rifts between people right on the eve of the war, and my question to you is: Was the emergence of ethnic parties in Bosnia and Herzegovina, didn't that emergence already lead to a certain ethnic rift in contrast with the previous life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, one could sense that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could one say that politics contributed to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all likelihood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what went on in the Bosnia and Herzegovian parliament? Could an agreement be reached on matters of fundamental importance, agreement among the parties who quit the parliament?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that representatives of the Serb people left the parliament of B and H?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if the Serbs organised a referendum and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that it was common knowledge that whenever a crisis would arise, then a Crisis Staff would be set up, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us then, when did those Crisis Staff were formed in the territory of B and H? Did all the three sides form them? When and where were they formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if any Crisis Staffs were formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crisis Staffs were formed after the Serbs had already taken over the power.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there any Crisis Staffs before the Serb side took over the power?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any Muslim or Croat Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the area of Puharska, was a Crisis Staff there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was when the weapons had to be handed over, when such existed, because it is common knowledge that there was Territorial Defence such as had been established before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that Crisis Staff in Puharska area was formed in November 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you that, because I didn't have any weapons, and I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that before the change of power took place in Prijedor that parties all voiced their programmes on radio -- on the radio in Prijedor, and you said that the SDS disseminated this propaganda, that one should go to Croatia and fight for Yugoslavia. Tell us, why do you consider that propaganda since at that time the SFRY was still in existence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: To me it was a fratricidal war. If I go somewhere else round Bosnia, then that was an aggression, to my mind, because we were the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina. There was nothing for us in Croatia. We had no business in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were you a citizen of Yugoslavia then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yugoslavia, I think, had already fallen apart. Bosnia was recognised by the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was before the recognition. My question refers to the period before the recognition.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I do not remember that. I do not think it was before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that during the interrogation in chief, that the Serbs had taken over the power in Prijedor on the 30th of April, 1992, and in view -- as you said that before the war, all the positions in Prijedor were in the hands of the SDA. I would like to ask you, since those parties did not and could not see eye-to-eye, wasn't it then natural that the key positions should be taken over by Serbs since they took over the authority there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they took over the power by force, by weapons, not in a referendum or in elections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And given the ethnic composition before the takeover of power on the part of the Serbs that all -- would it have been normal that all key positions be held by members of the same ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could -- would you consider that this may have been one of the reasons for the discontent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on the eve of the war, before the outbreak of the war, you did not leave Puharska. Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean before the breakout of the war? We had no war at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am referring to April, May, early June.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not a war that we had there at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the war, could you explain why you did not leave Puharska? I mean, this is what you had stated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say so. Because it was risky to move about town, because we had to pass through five or six checkpoints in order to arrive downtown, and at each checkpoint there were checks to determine your ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell me whether there was a control point at the entrance of Puharska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who held it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were controls there too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that various armed groups wearing different uniforms were moving about town. Were you able to identify them as the reservists or the active-duty JNA personnel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: One was not able to distinguish that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the age? Would you be able to distinguish by age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course you would have been able to distinguish it by age. What I mean is there were both younger and older among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you had heard that in late May, Keraterm was -- had -- was opened. Can you give us more details? How did you hear about it, who told you this, and what was the reason stated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I had some Serbs who were my neighbours and I would not like to go into that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't need to give us any names. Just tell us --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was from them that I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they tell you the reason why this was so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had their own opinion and the reasons were probably different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was their opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were neighbours and they had completely different opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just clarify? Did they -- they had completely different view of it in relation to whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to those who had opened up that camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber who opened this camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a fairly wide --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the local Serbs, I don't know exactly, but it is sort of a wide-ranging word.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are many Serbs in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot name the persons who opened this camp. Probably someone else knows this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that in early June you saw Serb soldiers coming to Puharska and searching houses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether, again, my question is: Were they active-duty personnel or reservists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was unable to distinguish the uniforms, that is active-duty uniforms versus reserve uniforms. You cannot distinguish the two. We lived in Yugoslavia, as you put it, and Yugoslavia had completely different uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these SMB uniforms, as we used to call them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were of different colours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these people from the Prijedor area or outside of Prijedor area, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew some men from Prijedor, but I guess that there were some others who were from outside, because I did not know them all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any difference in behaviour between the men from Prijedor and those who had come from outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any contact with them because I hid away from them when they came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that one Serb neighbour protected you from the arrest and that you hid away at his house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that you trusted him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why did you trust him, in view of the previous experiences which you mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we knew each other well and our views coincided. We agreed on our opinions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this Serb -- was this Serb in the military or somebody from his midst?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the military, but it was because he had to be with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you believe that there were many others who had to be in the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the situation that was in Bosnia, wasn't it true that a lot of people were not even asked whether they would -- they wanted to be in the military or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taking into account your last answer, we can -- could say that not all Serbs were the same in terms of their relation to other ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we agree on that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you had been called by telephone to report to the barracks. Could you tell me why did you volunteer to report that even though this person never introduced himself when he called you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I not reported, the person who had called me would probably show up with soldiers and then my family would have had problem in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 addition to me, because you could not hide anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your permission, I would like to ask the usher to give the witness a schedule which has already been tendered here as Exhibit number 19 and place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned two military police structures which you marked as "VP1" and "VP2" in the original. Could you tell us in some detail what this military police "1" was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what number "1" was because I was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this military police marked with "1", how far was that from the Keraterm compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the perimeter fence and the Banja Luka-Prijedor road separated it from the camp, and it was only -- it used to be a road maintenance facility -- company building before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that there was some kind of a headquarters there at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the vantage point, let's say in front of Rooms 1 and 2 in Keraterm, was there a visual contact between that point and the military police building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And conversely, persons who were in that building could see Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there, but probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I simply was asking whether there was any visual obstacles between the two areas.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could see them. I don't know if they could have seen us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons who were there, did they have a military police insignia or something that would distinguish them from the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had white belts that distinguished them from the other military personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now relative to the military police facility which you marked as "VP2" in the original, did they also have military police insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them. There were other soldiers among them too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area which you marked as "VP2"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And even civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see military policemen and these other individuals moving about the Keraterm compound freely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any fence between the area marked by "VP2" and the -- and where the inmates' rooms were or was there free access there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was just a small passage and there was all the railroad line which you had to cross and it was just a passageway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you show it to us on the sketch, because we cannot see it? Where was that passageway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The place that you're pointing at, can you tell us what the distance was between that passageway and the road? Approximately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately about 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was no obstacle of any kind there between these two areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there was a fence running alongside the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And between the "VP2"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means the area between the rooms as they are marked on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The access was free?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was nothing. It was just the old railroad tracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, when you were brought to the area marked as -- the building marked as "VP2", where did you come in, at what -- at which, gate? How did you get to the building marked "VP2"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please show us how you got there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could enter from the Banja Luka-Prijedor road, could you get in unobstructed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me one more thing about this sketch. Was this railroad track in front or behind the "VP2" building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you drew it on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately. The scale is not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that there was free access to that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These were old -- either a canteen or something else or maybe the dormitories for the workers of the ceramics building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what military was in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That building, "VP2".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me what colour that building was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were old wooden, makeshift buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this the right position of the building or is it more to the other side, towards the area marked as "X"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I couldn't tell you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall whether on the railroad track that is the area where the road intersects -- where the track intersects the road, was there a checkpoint there? That is to the right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand the question. I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me take you to the area in front of Rooms 1 and 2. Can you tell me whether there existed a kiosk at the gate at the entrance area which you marked as concrete tarmac, at the left corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a reception hut with scales. That was the scales for trucks which would come in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is fine, but the entrance gate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was also that, but I didn't mark it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you point to the Trial Chamber where that kiosk was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a guard there? a sentry? a soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say who was standing there because I never went up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, between the area marked as the scales and the barrel with water and green grassy area, was there another kiosk there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, the area in front of Room 1, was there anything there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Perhaps before my arrival there, but I do not recall anything being there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This is enough as far as the sketch is concerned. You said that after you came to the gate, two policemen in -- drove up to you in a Golf vehicle. My question to you is whether this vehicle had military police markings on them -- on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And it wasn't a military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These two men were not military policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said that Radetic questioned you, was he taking any notes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where exactly did he question you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: In his office, where he had his office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in the perimeter of the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was in what I marked as "VP2". From the barracks they brought me there to him, to Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any military police insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that after that, you went together to your house to get a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not him, no, not him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He sent some soldiers with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he perhaps say to you that your vehicle had been mobilised for the needs of the military?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not say that it was mobilised. He said that it was being confiscated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, apart from that situation, in view of the fact that you were a taxi driver, did you know that the law provided that in certain situations vehicles could be mobilised, passenger vehicles, freight vehicles, livestock?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not from one ethnic group only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about this legal provision?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not -- I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that in the -- the law provided that failure to comply with this requisition request was a criminal act?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given any receipt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever ask that this vehicle be returned to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When? I had no opportunity to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, after the interview was completed at "VP2", who escorted you to Keraterm, to the area in front of the rooms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of those guards. I don't know his name or anything about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The guard, was he a member of the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so, because he did not have the white belts. He wasn't wearing them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the military that were there with the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I did say that there were other soldiers there, in addition to the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was that military based? Where were they based?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they somewhere close to the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that when they took you to Keraterm, that you saw them beating inmates. Did you recognise anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: From among those who were beating them, no. There were -- these men were from around the -- around Prijedor, from Kozarac, Kozarusa, Biscani and those places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you just tell me, I forgot to ask you that in relation to the military police, which -- that you mentioned, when you were in front of the rooms, when you would come out to this area in front of the rooms, did you ever see soldiers who were not part of the security detail of your -- in other words, either the military policemen or some other soldiers who were moving about Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, and I didn't have enough time to observe that. I spent a very brief period of time with Radetic. I had no time to observe anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that after your arrival, you spoke to Zigic, and the situation that you mentioned was that it was while he was beating detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that scare you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know if Zoran Zigic had ever been arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the sketch, you marked room as the military prison next to Room 4. Were there any detainees in that facility and was it a military prison throughout your detention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you see anyone kept under custody there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a guy called Yugoslav who was there, a criminal from Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did, yes. But he moved about without any restraint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean as a detainee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you did your military service in Karlovac with engineers, if I'm correct. Did you -- after the service, did you become a member of the reserve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not have any combat orders or anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nor did you attend any military drill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you draw a parallel between the situation when you did your regular military service and the -- in terms of discipline, order, subordination and so on and so forth, and draw a parallel with the situation when you arrived in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was 100 per cent different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean there was no similarity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say it was 100 per cent different, that difference, do you mean it in the affirmative sense or an adverse sense?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: In an adverse sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us a while ago that you were frightened by Zigic's behaviour but he also advised you to go to Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm grateful to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you said that you found some room in the back of the dormitory under the wash-basin in Room 1; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that place also the result of his advice also?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the only place I could find because nobody wanted to sit under the wash-basin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you roughly tell us, from the door into Room 1, to the place where you were, could you roughly tell us what the length is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean in depth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any water in that wash-basin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Room 1, was there a barrel or something which was used by people to relieve themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, in a corner next to the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, people used it mostly at night because it was dangerous to go out, that is, ask somebody to go to the toilet, so that people --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me, from the place that you were in in the room and to the door, how many people were there between you and the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you name a figure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: A hundred, 150.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did people lie down or sit or move about or stand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depended on the time of the day and -- depends. One can't explain that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke about food, could you tell me, where was bread kept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bread was kept in those - what should I call them? - in plastic crates. It was brought there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were those plastic crates or plastic baskets kept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a room where bread was sliced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the prisoners slice that bread?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the prisoners distribute food too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, I think we've been over all this. It hasn't been disputed that the prisoners sliced the bread and distributed it. Unless it's a matter in dispute, there's no need to go over it again. Do you see?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I asked this question because other witnesses testified differently. That is the reason, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's not my recollection. Now, please let's move on. We've heard that there's a shortage of time. It's everybody's duty to move the case forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, were there any lights in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were searchlights which they had brought and mounted on a table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before those searchlights were brought, were there any lamp posts or something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were they in working order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: At times, yes; at times, no, because there were power cuts, power cuts in the town as a whole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it happen often, those power cuts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there were three guard shifts in Keraterm. So my question to you is: How long were those shifts? When did they change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I wouldn't be able to tell you that. I suppose they know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know when this three-shift system was established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was established prior to my arrival in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that shift commanders were Kole, Kajin, Fustar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Tomo Prodan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you used to see him around the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did he do there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On which shift?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke about Kajin, you said -- you described how you knew him and how you knew his father, and you said, "I thought we were friends." Could you tell us what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I know his entire family, and I'm sure that he knows me well. He's been to my house I don't know how many times, and I thought that we were friends. His father is a very good man, his brother is even better, and I know what -- what is this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did he ever harm you personally or do something unto you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not harm me, but he could have helped so that others wouldn't harm me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him help anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he helped me by calling the doctor to take me to the hospital. Not only me, but others too. Although he could have helped on other occasions. For instance, where Banovics beat me, he just walked past and never paid any attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what was his brother's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. No, I don't know what his nickname was, but I know he worked at a restaurant, that he was a waiter there, and we were good friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was his brother a guard in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he wasn't. Perhaps he came to visit him, but I don't think he was a guard. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that shift commanders were present during beatings. You described how those took place all over the camp in Keraterm, and you also said that there were no beatings during Kole's shift; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. Well, not as much as on other shifts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the battery room which you marked with "X" on your sketch, was it an isolated room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "isolated"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it isolated from all four sides? Was it fenced off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, its front side was open. It was a hangar or a car depot or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you refer to the presence, can you be more specific and explain what you mean by this, bearing in mind the number of prisoners in Keraterm, the size of the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "presence"? You mean the presence of shift commanders?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, also they were somewhere around. That is, they could lock the dormitories when they felt like it, and when they didn't, they just left them open. But they were around or they would simply vanish somewhere. They would simply leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is why I'm asking you. When you say "present," does this mean that he is present in the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they would be present, for instance, when the food was distributed, and that is when they usually beat us, when food was distributed, or they would line us up and beat us there. They were present there, for instance, during the readouts, they would line us up as if supposedly they were taking some people to Trnopolje, some of the elderly people, but they were present there. That is they were -- at those times, they were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific, they are beating somebody in front of Room 1 and in Room "X", for instance, would the shift commander then, according to you, be present there if he is somewhere in the Keraterm area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally he is, because he allowed those men to enter the Keraterm compound, which means that he is present, he's an accomplice. If you allow somebody to enter, that means that you know that he is there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that he allowed them to enter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: How else did they enter?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The persons that you indicated, Zigic, Duca, Timarac, did they enter Keraterm freely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yup.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did somebody ever stop them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could anyone stop them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who, to your mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? Which gentlemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: The accused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when there was some fire exchanged between guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, when you were taken to the investigator for interrogation, could you explain the status of investigators in relation to guards? Was he superior to them or subordinate to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, what investigator?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The interrogators on the upper floor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all by themselves in those offices and those were merely formalities that -- the date of birth, name, your ethnic background, what do you think about the situation, and such like. They could not be called mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But to your mind, were there -- did they rank higher than the guards in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say that. I do not know. But I think that it was they nevertheless who compiled those lists, the lists of 120 names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But could you tell us when you would be taken to this investigator, which way would they take you up to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, which way?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, they take you out of Room 1, behind the room there was a passage and then stairways leading to the upper floor. And as for the time that you spent at Keraterm, could you give us the dates which stuck in your memory which you still remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dates?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you give us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 12th June I was taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean arrested? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, arrested. The 5th of July is when I was beaten. On the 7th of July, taken to the hospital. On the 24th of July, the first massacre. On the 25th of July, the second massacre. On the 8th of August, Keraterm disbanded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you leave Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it was disbanded and it was the last day for all of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the 8th of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the 5th of July as the date on which you were beaten by Zigic, Duca, Vokic, Timarac and some other men whom you did not know and were present there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. I knew another one whom you didn't mention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean Karlica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did it happen in that room which you marked with "X"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that on that occasion, Fustar's shift was on duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Fustar present when it happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think not. I think he was somewhere in the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It means that he was present within the compound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that in the hospital you were interrogated by military investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you returned to Keraterm, you then -- you again said that persons who had beaten you kept coming to the -- to the place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that no sanctions were undertaken against them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you think, why was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: For what?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That no sanctions were applied to them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say that. What are you trying to prove, that somebody was afraid of them?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not trying to prove anything. I'm just asking.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness F, was there some kind of a sentry gate through which persons entering the camp had to pass and where they would be checked before entering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It was manned by who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was manned by camp guards, by the guards of Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we could get food from our families, and the guards at the gate would take this food or, rather, those bags with food and would look through them and keep whatever that was good in them and the rest they just threw on the garbage dump.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Rodic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever talk with Kajin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever approach him to ask him something in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, because I was afraid. I didn't know how he would react. Because it would have been natural for him to come to me since I was in a worse situation than he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no doubt that you were in a worse situation, but in view of the number of people there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well -- but he did see me about. He knew that I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he talk with the foreman of your room, the man who was made responsible for Room 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that every room had its foreman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who it was in your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was somebody called Brta or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he the one who communicated with the shift commanders on a more or less regular basis also?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Kajin organised help, that is, organised a visit to the doctor.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that as his attempt to protect people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose so. He saw what the situation was in the room, because there were so many living dead there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But could somebody else realise the situation before him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the second day after -- yes, of course they could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did anyone ever undertake anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then, could one take this as his -- as the effort he made to help you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can we then take it that he disagreed with the fact that somebody beat you or that other people were beaten? He didn't just gloss over that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, possibly, yes, but he must have realised already that he would be proclaimed a war --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do not say anything.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think he was already aware --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he was aware that he would be proclaimed a war criminal, because it did happen from time to time that he did have one too many, that he'd come to us, begin to cry and say that this would happen. I mean, he was aware of that. But at any rate, be that as it may, I mean he did help us by doing what he did to have us moved to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know why did he cry and where would he come on such occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he would come to the door of the dormitory at night, and I suppose when all of a sudden he'd feel bad and he'd come over to talk with us, and that was that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are at the time when we take a break. You must try to complete your cross-examination as quickly as possible. How much longer do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 15 minutes or so after the break then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll take the break now and we'll resume at 11.30. Witness F, I remind you not to discuss your evidence with anyone during the break, including members of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you check on the translation. Would you start again.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not all answers were -- appeared on the record, so I would just like to make two or three follow-up questions just for him to be able to give answers. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness F, is it true that you said that after you were beaten that nobody gave you assistance even though people were able to see and were in a position to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact that Kajin organised medical care, you said that in this way he had protected you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All injured persons were examined by a doctor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Kajin frequently came and talked to the inmates and said that he was sorry that all this was happening, because he was friends with a lot of you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that on these occasions, it happened that he was crying while he was there with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I would like the assistance of the usher, please, to show the Witness F the appropriate medical records that are referred to him. And we also have sufficient number of copies for Their Honours. The Prosecution and the parties have been provided with the copies of this earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, to just check the name, the date of birth, and is that identical with your date? In fact, first you have the translation and then it will be the original.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no translation here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please check all the pages that you have.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that refer to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see both my last name and the date of birth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that data appear on each of the pages of the document or each of the versions of the document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the first and last name, yes, but I was not taken to the hospital on the 1st of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. We will ask you that. But we are in agreement on the data, the personal data?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is also an excerpt from the hospital registry reflecting your reception in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why does it say Ljubija? I was never --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the name and the birth year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says detainee from Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but everything is crossed out. It seems like it was written and then erased again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then next you have the history of -- or the -- of condition for Witness F. It is this document, and it states both Puharska and prisoner from Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- prisoner? What does --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prisoner from Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a camp inmate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just reading what is stated there. There is also a referral of the specialist bearing your name there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Again, first, last name, and birth year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This release letter from the hospital, it also refers to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there again, only the year of birth and the name is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Puharska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please let me ask you the appropriate questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned 5th of July as the date when you were beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your discharge document and your the letter of your reception, it states that you were treated between the 1st and the 9th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is wrong. I was beaten on the 5th. I was taken to the hospital on the 7th, and I stayed there for about ten days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you explain this, this date, both the -- both these documents reflect the 1st. Could it be that you were taken to the hospital on the 1st and that you had been beaten two days before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct. I was beaten on the 5th. I couldn't have been taken to the hospital before having been beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you allow for a mistake in the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I wasn't there about these eight days but about ten days, and I know who was with me in the hospital and who these men were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would -- I tender the medical records for the witness into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I would just like to remind Mr. Rodic and the other Defence counsel that what I said about producing exhibits in the two working languages applies equally to them, and it also applies to documents that are produced in court as potential exhibits, as documents which may or may not become exhibits. But certainly where you intend to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 25 produce a document as an exhibit, it is to be in the two working languages. Yes, Ms. Baly?

utterances.speaker: MS. BALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have no objection to the admission of this document. We do note, however, that it does name the witness and we would ask that it be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It will be under seal for that reason, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit D1/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether on that occasion, were the two Ganic men, a father and a son, were taken to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And anyone else that you knew by name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you name them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eso Islamovic, a policeman from Ljubija, was there with me, and a 16 year old boy, Alisic, Admir or Almir and there was also an Albanian man, and there were the Edin and Abaz Ganic, a son and a father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me now, during your examination-in-chief you said that you had been beaten in the hospital too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us any details about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the hospital we had a guard in front of our room, and also there were guards who were outside under the windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these soldiers or policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you had a guard in front of the room, how could it happen that somebody would beat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a silly question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is not a silly question. This is a question I ask you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guards let them in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you complain to anyone at the hospital? Did anyone intervene?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not complain to anyone because we did not know to whom, and also, we did not dare. To whom were we to have complained? We were happy to have been brought to the hospital at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the injuries that you sustained, do you believe that your life was saved by the fact that you were brought to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just quickly I want to ask you something else. You said that you were beaten by the Banovic brothers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether this happened before your hospitalisation or after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS F [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened after I came back from the hospital. We were lined up for the food and water and this is when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm finished. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
