utterances.text: And the name is Arifagic, Abdul Enver. Is that a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his relationship to you?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: His father and my father were cousins. They were sons of two brothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is a date at the bottom there, 21/08/1992, Vlasic. Do you know what that refers to?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: It refers to the Vlasic case. During my stay in Trnopolje camp, Enver arrived at the Trnopolje camp. He had been transferred from Omarska. During the organisation of this convoy that was -- that had crossed Vlasic, Enver was a very wealthy man. He had worked in Switzerland for a long period of time and had retired. He had a good house, good car and everything else. Before his departure, he told me that he had transferred his car to a Serb in Prijedor, I don't know whom, and that he had arranged with him to be on this -- to be on this convoy that was crossing Mount Vlasic. He never emerged on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether he has ever been seen by any member of your family since the 21st of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: No, nobody ever -- nobody has ever seen him. I think that his sons - and they are still in Switzerland - through a Serb friend in Switzerland, he had promised them to -- that he would find him for a great deal of money, and he disappeared and the money disappeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I just want to find out --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I'm not trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- that last date, then, is the date last seen or the date of death?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: That is what I was trying to do. And for the next one I thought I would ask the witness, if we could turn quickly to number 150 on the same page, Arifagic, Arif Hamdija. There is a date there, 20/07/1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't need the details of the individual, sir, but what does that date refer to? Do you see --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: On that date, Hamdija was taken from Omarska. He was an active-duty police officer, and he was -- spent his entire career in Omarska. The explanation was that he had been taken to be exchanged but nobody ever saw him again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, is he alive today?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vucicevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUCICEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to stipulate to this exhibit, and I respectfully suggest that the exhibit speaks for itself with the dates that are therein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think you need to do any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I thought I'd try a couple.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, these are the people that you marked in the book and these are the ones that are highlighted in yellow. Could you perhaps just quickly look at the copy that we have made?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Could you show him the copy that's been given to counsel?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there yellow highlights there, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those yellow highlights correspond with your family relatives; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. Those are the questions I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: What I would like to add is that some of the members of my family have been exhumed. They were found in mass graves and subsequently identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. I'd like to ask you two questions. Firstly, in the early parts of your testimony, you gave evidence of three fingers being broken, which were never set. What is the state of those fingers today? Were they ever set? And if so, when and where?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: The first examination, that is the adequate examination which I received, was when I arrived in the transit centre at Karlovac. The physicians -- the first physicians who were there registered that case. After that, it healed. They took X-rays. And probably part of the tendons -- I don't know, but now I can move my fingers. However, if I exert my arm a little bit more, I lose strength in it quite quickly and I cannot use it properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When did you arrive at Karlovac?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: The 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So you spent the rest of your --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You spent the rest of your time at Keraterm with your fingers broken?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Was it brought to the attention of anybody that your fingers were broken?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: To whom I draw attention? There were people with worse injuries, with broken hips. If you wanted to draw attention to your injury, you would end up in a truck where you were asked to provide help, and you would never appear again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... with Sikirica. I believe you gave evidence that after the second massacre, which was the day after the first, you saw him when the bodies were being removed. Did you see him at any time at Keraterm after that and prior to your leaving?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That was the moment I remember quite well. It was one, two or three days before the camp was disbanded. We were ordered to bring out all the pallets where we had slept, to wash the room and the pallets, and we thought that it was a day when the camp would be disbanded. However, all this was returned and we stayed there. And then a day or two before the camp was disbanded, we were lined up. Again it was in front of the Room 1, closer to the road. Kajin was there and he was counting us, Sikirica was on the side, and I know that all of those who were counting inmates were going to him with these lists, and they were all addressing him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you see him again at Keraterm after that, prior to your leaving?

utterances.speaker: JUSUF ARIFAGIC
utterances.text: I think that I did not. It was disbanded right after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We will now take the adjournment and resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning. Mr. Arifagic, you're reminded not to discuss your evidence with anyone, including members of the Prosecution team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 5.13 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday the 3rd day of April, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
